contexts.text: To water the garden () = to give intelligence. AE 518:14.
Well-watered () = that goods and truths can grow there.
To water the mountains () = to bless those who are in love to the Lord and towards the neighbour.

Their soul shall be as a watered garden... I will water the weary soul, and every soul that is sorrowful ()... To be watered = to be instructed. ( = that such have intelligence and wisdom from this source. AE 374:3.)
He watereth the mountains from His chambers () = that all goods [come] through truths from Heaven. To water is predicated of truths, because waters = truths.

A fountain shall go forth from the house of Jehovah, and shall water the stream of Shittim () = that out of Heaven from the Lord there will be truth of doctrine which will enlighten those who are in knowledges.
To water the earth, and to make it bring forth and bud () = to vivify the Church, that it may bring forth the truth of doctrine and of faith, and the good of love and charity.
To water its furrows... () = to fill with the Knowledges of good and truth.

To water the earth () = to fertilize the Church, which is said to be fertilized when truths are multiplied, causing an increase of intelligence; and when goods are fructified, causing an increase of heavenly love.
